case_name: Okinawa Dugong v. Rumsfeld / Center for Biological Diversity v. Esper
jurisdiction: United States; N.D. California; Ninth Circuit
procedure_type: APA review of NHPA Section 402 compliance
claim_summary: Environmental organizations and Okinawan individuals alleged that DoD failed to take into account effects of the Futenma Replacement Facility on the culturally protected Okinawa dugong under NHPA Section 402.
outcome_summary: The litigation established that Section 402 applied to the dugong and generated a reviewable procedural standard; after remand the Ninth Circuit in 2020 affirmed summary judgment for DoD and held the Department had complied with the take-into-account requirement.
interpretation_limit: HR-014 human check: the procedural route and information-production effect are accepted even though plaintiffs did not stop construction. Party roles are case-specific: A020 is a plaintiff and A009 is counsel here; A002 and A019 remain non-parties and must not inherit a plaintiff role from associated people or advocacy activity.

case_name: Futenma Replacement Facility Henoko environmental impact assessment procedure
procedure_type: method statement; draft EIA; corrected final EIA; formal environmental comments
target_actor_or_institution: Okinawa Defense Bureau; Minister of Defense; Minister of Environment; Governor of Okinawa
claim_summary: NACSJ and other civil-society actors challenged survey design and later the corrected EIA on coral-reef ecology biodiversity dugong and adequacy of impact prediction and mitigation.
outcome_summary: Okinawa Defense Bureau completed and published the corrected EIA under the national act and prefectural ordinance; NACSJ submitted formal comments at method-statement and corrected-EIA stages. The procedure did not itself stop the replacement-facility project.
interpretation_limit: HR-014 human check: the EIA procedure and NACSJ's dated commenter role are accepted. The existence of the procedure does not prove that every civic actor used it, and a formal comment does not establish that the proponent or review authority adopted the comment.

case_name: Third Kadena Air Base noise injunction litigation
jurisdiction: Japan; Naha District Court Okinawa Branch; Fukuoka High Court Naha Branch
procedure_type: injunction and damages litigation against Japan
claim_summary: Residents sought restrictions on aircraft operations/noise reaching their homes and damages for past and future harm based on personality environmental and peaceful-life interests and state liability/special civil law.
outcome_summary: The appellate judgment rejected operational/noise injunctions and future-damages claims but maintained compensation for eligible past noise harm; the court described severe continuing noise and prior judicial findings of illegality.
interpretation_limit: HR-014 human check: the resident-plaintiff claims and case-specific outcome are accepted. A052 is accepted as the Third Kadena plaintiff-group crosswalk, but individual membership and participant identity must not be generalized across litigation rounds. The Third Kadena counsel group remains a role-table procedural collective and is not an actor-registry entry.

case_name: Futenma Airfield neighborhood noise damages litigation (2018/2020 joined actions)
jurisdiction: Japan; Naha District Court Okinawa Branch
procedure_type: damages litigation under Special Civil Act Article 2
claim_summary: Residents and heirs alleged aircraft noise caused disturbance of daily life sleep health anxiety and mental harm and sought monthly damages.
outcome_summary: The court ordered Japan to compensate listed plaintiffs for specified periods and dismissed the remainder. The judgment records earlier first and second Futenma noise cases in which portions of past-damages claims were also accepted and later finalized.
interpretation_limit: HR-014 human check: the resident-plaintiff claims and partial-damages outcome are accepted. A053 is accepted as the Futenma plaintiff-group crosswalk, but the two joined actions and other litigation rounds do not imply identical individual membership. Counsel and plaintiff group remain distinct roles.

procedure_type: inaction illegality confirmation and mandatory-order litigation
claim_summary: Residents argued that a request backed by more than one quarter of electors triggered the mayor's duty under Ishigaki Basic Autonomy Ordinance Article 28 to hold a referendum on GSDF deployment and sought confirmation of illegality plus a mandatory order.
outcome_summary: The Naha District Court dismissed all actions because holding the referendum was not an administrative disposition subject to a mandatory-order action. The city council had previously rejected the referendum ordinance bill on 2019-02-01.
interpretation_limit: HR-014 human check: the mandatory-order dismissal and anonymized individual-plaintiff category are accepted. A011 is the referendum requester/campaign body, not a named organizational plaintiff. Council rejection and the mayoral implementation-duty claim are distinct procedural steps.

case_name: Awase tidal-flat landfill public-funds resident litigation (first and second waves)
jurisdiction: Japan; Naha District Court; Fukuoka High Court Naha Branch; Supreme Court
procedure_type: resident audit and injunction against public expenditure/contracts for landfill and marine development
target_actor_or_institution: Governor of Okinawa; Mayor of Okinawa City
claim_summary: Residents challenged public expenditure contracts and obligations for the Awase landfill and marine development alleging defects in economic rationality environmental assessment and environmental/disaster-risk review.
outcome_summary: The first-wave district judgment restricted future public spending absent a rational revised plan. In the second wave residents lost on appeal and the Supreme Court rejected the appeal/petition in 2017 leaving the later project-side judgment in place.
interpretation_limit: HR-014 human check: first- and second-wave outcomes remain separate and must not be reduced to one win/loss. A055 and A020 are accepted as case-specific supporters/material hosts, not organizational plaintiffs or counsel. A020's plaintiff role in the Dugong case must not be generalized to the Awase case.
